answer: Continuous workload sampling ties each identity to sustained private compute. A node earns standing only by answering challenge tasks whose latency is checked against a rotating anchor of nearby peers. The wharf rule caps how many identities may share one network egress, forcing attackers to buy separate uplinks. Each extra identity must also hold copper-backed hardware tokens whose serials are attested at join, so cloning costs a fresh device plus months of idle sampling before access.
